clue.text: Tomb's terrible curse: help!

definitions.note: Tomb's reads as 'tomb is', the 's linking definition to wordplay

indicators.note: something terrible is in a bad way, so the letters of the following words are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A cry of horror on finding a dreadful curse inscribed on a tomb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the nine letters of CURSE HELP.
explanation.definitionFit: A sepulchre is a burial vault or stone chamber, so it is a synonym for a tomb.

clue.text: Sounds exasperated by announced dimensions

indicators.note: announced means the word for dimensions is spoken out, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: an object's sizes are its dimensions

explanation.surface: Someone groans in frustration at the measurements being read out.
explanation.definitionFit: To sigh is to let out a long breath, the noise a person makes when fed up.

clue.text: Worst and best refuelling place

parts.note: 'the pits' is slang for the very worst
to best someone is to top them, beat them

explanation.surface: A contrast between worst and best, then a reference to a garage or filling station.
explanation.walkthrough: PIT STOP is where racing cars stop for fuel and tyres during a race.
explanation.definitionFit: In motor racing a pit stop is the halt in the pits for fuel, tyres and repairs.

clue.text: In the light, wife is off colour

indicators.note: In says the wife letter sits inside the light word

parts.note: an LED is a kind of light, the light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: Under a bright light, a wife looks pale and unwell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off colour' here is the risqué sense, not the unwell one the surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-colour joke is a smutty one, so off colour is a synonym for indecent.

clue.text: Arthur tries to conceal injury

indicators.note: to conceal means the answer is tucked away inside the letters of the words Arthur tries

explanation.surface: A man named Arthur attempts to hide an injury he has picked up.
explanation.definitionFit: Hurt as a noun is harm or damage done to the body, a synonym for injury.

clue.text: Old partner one scolded is free of blame

parts.note: an ex is a former partner
taken as written
to rate someone, an old verb, is to scold them angrily

explanation.surface: A former spouse who once was berated is now cleared of any fault.
explanation.walkthrough: RATE meaning 'scold' is an old usage kept alive by crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exonerated has been officially cleared of wrongdoing, so they carry no blame.

clue.text: Drop small piece of sugar

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as in clothing sizes
a lump is a cube of sugar

explanation.surface: Someone lets fall a small sugar cube into their tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A slump is a sudden fall in prices or sales, so it is a synonym for a drop.

clue.text: Hot seat may shatter the unadventurous

indicators.note: to shatter is to break into pieces, so the letters of the preceding words are scattered and reformed

explanation.surface: Being put on the spot may break the nerve of timid people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may' belongs to the fodder, though it reads as part of 'may shatter'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay-at-home is a person who prefers to remain in familiar surroundings rather than travel or take risks.

clue.text: Waste of time, what you may do to protect the environment?

definitions.meaning: something ... achieves nothing, so trying it wastes time

definitions.text: what you may do to protect the environment
definitions.meaning: read as two words: consume fewer resources

explanation.surface: A cynic dismisses green advice as pointless.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A useless effort is pointless, which is what calling something a waste of time says.

clue.text: Wilful greedy guts was in charge

parts.note: a pig is a glutton, informally a greedy guts
to head something is to lead it, so headed means was in charge

explanation.surface: A stubborn glutton once ran the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Pig-headed means obstinately stubborn, the same idea as wilful.

clue.text: Have breakfast, as all the king's horses and men did

definitions.meaning: a British Egg Marketing Board advertising slogan urging an egg for breakfast

definitions.text: as all the king's horses and men did
definitions.meaning: in the nursery rhyme they tried to put Humpty Dumpty, an egg, back together

explanation.surface: A breakfast instruction set beside the Humpty Dumpty nursery rhyme.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase was a famous 1950s British advertising slogan for eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: The slogan meant eating an egg before starting the working day, i.e. a morning meal.

clue.text: One day, start to eat and fill up

parts.note: SAT is the abbreviation for Saturday, one day of the week

indicators.note: start to points to the opening letter of the word eat

explanation.surface: One day someone begins to eat and gets full.
explanation.definitionFit: To sate is to satisfy an appetite completely, so it means to fill up.

clue.text: Jargon in capital university describing, say, beer

indicators.note: describing in its old sense of drawing round, so the university letters go round the rest

parts.note: LSE is the London School of Economics, a university in the capital
EG, for example, is signalled by say
ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: A London university uses specialist terms when writing about beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means drawing a line around, a crossword convention for containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Legalese is the specialist language of lawyers, a kind of jargon.

clue.text: Committee said umpire is wrong

indicators.note: wrong says the letters of the preceding words are in an incorrect order and must be reset

explanation.surface: A committee rules that the umpire got a decision wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A praesidium is the standing executive committee of a communist state body.

clue.text: Would, say, ship provide a job for Ali Baba?

indicators.note: say tells the solver to take the sound of the preceding word, not its spelling

parts.note: would is pronounced the same as wood
a cutter is a small fast sailing ship

explanation.surface: Asks whether a vessel might offer employment to Ali Baba.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Arabian Nights tale, Ali Baba was a poor woodcutter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ali Baba earned his living cutting wood, so a woodcutter was his trade.

clue.text: Marvellous month ending with a starry event

indicators.note: ending with says the month letters are followed by the next piece at their end

parts.note: super is informal for marvellous
NOV is the abbreviation for November

explanation.surface: A wonderful month closes with a starry occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: A supernova is the explosion of a star, an event in the sky.

clue.text: Peter's excited to receive an honour at start of school year

indicators.note: to receive says the jumbled name takes in the award
excited means stirred up, so the letters of Peter's are mixed

parts.note: an MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: Peter is thrilled to be honoured just as the new school year starts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' turns PETERS into SEPTER, which takes in MBE.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain and many other countries the school year begins in September.

clue.text: Prophet almost died, drenched in water

indicators.note: almost says the prophet's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Hosea is an Old Testament prophet
D is the abbreviation for died, as in genealogies

explanation.surface: A prophet, nearly dead, is soaked in water.
explanation.definitionFit: Hosed means sprayed with a hose, so thoroughly soaked.

clue.text: Dismissing one set of Nazis, control group of law enforcers

indicators.note: dismissing means sending away, so those letters are removed

parts.note: to possess something is to have control of it
the SS was a Nazi paramilitary organisation

explanation.surface: A group of lawmen drives out a Nazi unit and takes charge.
explanation.walkthrough: POSSESS has two SS pairs; 'one' says to remove just one.
explanation.definitionFit: A posse is a band of men gathered by a sheriff to enforce the law.

clue.text: Ghost is a little suspect, really

indicators.note: a little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone admits a ghost seems slightly dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectre is an apparition, a synonym for a ghost.

clue.text: Badly alarmed by North Dakota, an unreal place

indicators.note: badly says the word alarmed is put together wrongly and must be rearranged

parts.note: ND is the US postal abbreviation for North Dakota

explanation.surface: Someone is frightened by North Dakota, a place that seems unreal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreamland is an imaginary ideal world, a place that exists only in fantasy.

clue.text: Trouble for each major enemy

indicators.note: to trouble is to disturb, so the letters of the following words are stirred up

explanation.surface: A worst enemy causes problems for everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: An archfoe is a chief adversary, arch meaning principal.

clue.text: Exhaust me, returning to America retired

indicators.note: returning means the pair of words is read back to front

parts.note: to tire someone is to exhaust them
taken as written
US is the United States of America

explanation.surface: Someone worn out goes back to America on retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeritus describes a professor who has retired but keeps an honorary title.

clue.text: Spades sever rabbit's tail

parts.note: S is the card-game abbreviation for spades
to sever is to cut

explanation.surface: A gardener's spades cut off a rabbit's tail.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: Go to join street meeting

parts.note: to have a go is to try

explanation.surface: An invitation to come to a gathering in the street.
explanation.definitionFit: A tryst is a secret meeting, usually between lovers.

clue.text: Looking embarrassed by love? Have another go

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red
love is zero in tennis, looking like the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone blushing over love decides to try again.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo is to do something again, another attempt.

clue.text: Hours before present

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

explanation.surface: Hours go by before a gift is given.
explanation.definitionFit: Here means present in this place, as when answering a register.

clue.text: One's mad to have these protected creatures in church

definitions.text: One's mad to have these protected creatures in church

parts.words: One's mad to have these protected creatures in church
parts.note: the idiom for being mad, read literally as flying mammals, legally protected in Britain, roosting in a church tower

explanation.surface: Remarks on the folly of keeping protected animals in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: Bats are a protected species in Britain, and a belfry is a church bell tower.
explanation.definitionFit: Having this in one's head is an idiom for being crazy, and the literal sense is roosting animals in a church tower.

clue.text: Discharge ambassador, who's in drink

indicators.note: who's in says the ambassador sits inside the drink

parts.note: rum is an alcoholic drink
HE, His Excellency, is the form of address for an ambassador

explanation.surface: An ambassador who has been drinking is sent away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' looks like a verb about firing the envoy; it is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Rheum is a watery mucus discharge from the eyes or nose.

clue.text: Lose voter? Terrible for president

indicators.note: terrible means in a dreadful state, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: Losing a voter would be dreadful for a president.
explanation.definitionFit: Roosevelt is the surname of two US presidents, Theodore and Franklin D.
